announcement.name: BUS230 Assessment 2 – Final LMS Submission Reminder
announcement.message:
Hi everyone,

As we are now halfway through the live presentations for Assessment 2 being completed, I wanted to share a few important reminders for your final LMS submission.

Please do not edit the presentation slides

The presentation delivered in class is recorded, including the slides shown on the day.

Please therefore submit the same presentation that you deliver live, without changing, adding, removing or improving any of the slide content after the presentation.

This is important so that the material submitted to the LMS is consistent with the presentation that was actually recorded as a part of the assessment. Making changes to the presentation after it has been delivered could raise academic integrity concerns.

You MUST ensure that the required academic notes supporting the existing slides are included with your submission.

Academic notes

As discussed in class, the brief points shown on your slides should be supported by fuller academic explanation.

For each relevant slide, your academic notes should be about a paragraph or two in order to:

  • explain the point or claim made on the slide in more detail;

  • provide the academic evidence supporting it;

  • include the relevant in-text citations;

  • explain the reasoning behind your analysis, limitations and proposed modification where relevant; and

  • clearly correspond to the content already presented on that slide.

The Unit Outline allows this additional academic explanation to be provided either in the presentation Notes section or as a separate supporting document.

If you use a separate document, please clearly identify the slide number before the corresponding notes, for example:

  • Slide 7 – Limitation 1
    Academic explanation and supporting citations...
  • Slide 8 – Limitation 2
    Academic explanation and supporting citations...

The academic notes should support the slides you already presented, not introduce new arguments, limitations, modifications, evidence or content that was not part of the presentation.

Academic notes are not your speaking notes

Please remember that these are different from the personal speaking notes you may have used during the presentation.

Your academic notes provide the research, evidence and explanation behind the slide content. Your speaking notes were simply there to help you deliver the presentation and do not need to be submitted as the academic supporting notes.

Before submitting

Please check that:

  • the presentation itself is the same version that was presented in class;

  • the academic notes clearly correspond to the relevant slides;

  • academic claims are supported with appropriate in-text citations;

  • your reference list matches the sources cited in the presentation and academic notes; and

  • you have not added new substantive content to the presentation after the live assessment.

This will ensure that the LMS submission accurately reflects the work that was presented and assessed on the day.

All the best.

Best,
Shahinda
